Section 4.1. The Board of Governors shall be the highest governing body of the Consortium. The Board shall comprise representatives of member institutions, with each full member entitled to one seat.

Section 4.3. The Executive Committee, comprising the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, and three additional Board members, shall manage the day-to-day affairs of the Consortium between Board meetings.

Section 4.4. The Secretariat, headed by an Executive Director, shall provide administrative support and maintain the official records of the Consortium.

Section 4.5. Standing committees may be established by the Board, including (but not limited to) the Scientific Review Committee, the Site Operations Committee, the Data Safety Monitoring Committee, and the Finance and Audit Committee.

ARTICLE V — MEETINGS

Section 5.1. The Board shall meet at least twice annually. Additional meetings may be convened by the Chairperson or upon the written request of at least one-third of the members.

Section 5.2. Notice of meetings shall be given to all members at least fourteen days in advance, except in cases of emergency where shorter notice may be given.

Section 5.3. A quorum shall consist of a majority of the Board members. Decisions shall be made by majority vote unless otherwise specified in this Charter.

Section 6.1. The Consortium shall be funded through membership fees, grants, research contracts, and other lawful sources.

Section 7.1. This Charter may be amended by a two-thirds vote of the Board, provided that notice of the proposed amendment has been circulated to members at least thirty days in advance of the meeting.

In the event of dissolution, the assets of the Consortium shall be applied first to settle outstanding obligations, and any remainder shall be transferred to charitable or research organisations with similar purposes, as determined by the Board.

The Board noted the recommendation of the Governance Sub-Committee regarding the proposed amendment to Clause 9.2 (Quorum) of the Charter. The Sub-Committee met on 6 May 2020 and considered the proposal raised by Prof. Ng at the 16 April 2020 meeting. The Sub-Committee's report was circulated to all Board members on 8 May 2020.

The Sub-Committee recommended that the quorum requirement be revised from two-thirds of Board members to a simple majority, subject to the condition that at least one member is physically present at the Consortium's premises. This recommendation was reached by a majority of four to one, with Dr. Yusof dissenting. Dr. Yusof maintained his position that a lower quorum could weaken decision-making for matters requiring a two-thirds majority vote, such as amendments to the Charter itself or the removal of a Board member.

The Board discussed the report at length. Prof. Lee noted that the Charter's electronic voting provisions (Clause 9.4) had been used successfully for the first time during the 16 April 2020 meeting and that this experience supported the case for a lower quorum. Prof. Ng added that the ongoing COVID-19 situation made it impractical to convene two-thirds of members physically in the near term.

**Resolution 2020-07: The Board approved the amendment to Clause 9.2, effective 1 June 2020. The amended clause reads: "A quorum shall consist of a simple majority of Board members, provided that at least one member is physically present at the Consortium's premises or at a location designated by the Chair. Matters requiring a two-thirds majority vote under this Charter shall require the affirmative vote of two-thirds of all Board members, regardless of the number present."**

Section 3.2. Applications for membership shall be reviewed by the Secretariat and recommended to the Board for approval. Admission requires a two-thirds vote of the Board.

Section 3.3. Member institutions shall designate a Principal Investigator and an Institutional Representative to act on their behalf in Consortium matters.

Section 3.4. Membership may be terminated by resignation, by dissolution of the member institution, or by resolution of the Board for cause, following an opportunity for the member to be heard.

ARTICLE IV — GOVERNING STRUCTURE

Section 4.1. The Board of Governors shall be the highest governing body of the Consortium. The Board shall comprise representatives of member institutions, with each full member entitled to one seat.

Section 4.2. The Board shall elect from among its members a Chairperson and a Vice-Chairperson, each for a term of two years, renewable once.

Section 4.3. The Executive Committee, comprising the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, and three additional Board members, shall manage the day-to-day affairs of the Consortium between Board meetings.

Section 4.4. The Secretariat, headed by an Executive Director, shall provide administrative support and maintain the official records of the Consortium.

Section 4.5. Standing committees may be established by the Board, including (but not limited to) the Scientific Review Committee, the Site Operations Committee, the Data Safety Monitoring Committee, and the Finance and Audit Committee.

ARTICLE V — MEETINGS

Section 5.1. The Board shall meet at least twice annually. Additional meetings may be convened by the Chairperson or upon the written request of at least one-third of the members.

Section 5.2. Notice of meetings shall be given to all members at least fourteen days in advance, except in cases of emergency where shorter notice may be given.

Section 5.3. A quorum shall consist of a majority of the Board members. Decisions shall be made by majority vote unless otherwise specified in this Charter.

Meridian Oncology Research Consortium established_on 2018-03-15 date. Record status: current.

Section 5.4. Minutes of all meetings shall be recorded and maintained by the Secretariat, and shall be made available to members upon request.

ARTICLE VI — FINANCE

Section 6.1. The Consortium shall be funded through membership fees, grants, research contracts, and other lawful sources.

Section 6.2. The fiscal year shall run from 1 April to 31 March.

Section 6.3. The Finance and Audit Committee shall oversee the preparation of budgets and financial statements, and shall recommend external auditors for appointment by the Board.

ARTICLE VII — AMENDMENTS

Section 7.1. This Charter may be amended by a two-thirds vote of the Board, provided that notice of the proposed amendment has been circulated to members at least thirty days in advance of the meeting.

Section 7.2. Amendments shall take effect immediately upon adoption, unless the amendment resolution specifies a later effective date.

ARTICLE VIII — DISSOLUTION

In the event of dissolution, the assets of the Consortium shall be applied first to settle outstanding obligations, and any remainder shall be transferred to charitable or research organisations with similar purposes, as determined by the Board.

---

ADOPTION OF CHARTER

The foregoing Charter was adopted by the founding members on 15 March 2018, the date of establishment of the Consortium.

   Minutes of the meeting held on 6 February 2020 were approved without amendment. Dr. Tan noted that the action item on updating the vendor due diligence checklist was still open and requested completion by end of March.

2. Review of the Consortium's Delegation of Authority (DoA) Policy
   Mr. Wong presented a revised draft of the DoA Policy, v2.0. Key changes compared to v1.3 (dated 2018) include:
   - Raising the threshold for non-budgeted expenditure requiring Executive Director approval from S$10,000 to S$15,000.
   - Clarifying that the Head of Clinical Operations may approve protocol amendments up to S$25,000 per site, subject to the amendment not involving a change to the primary endpoint.
   - Adding a provision that all deviations from the DoA must be logged in the central register within five (5) working days.

Discussion: Dr. Lim raised a concern that the new threshold for protocol amendments might not be sufficient for multi-site global studies, but she agreed to defer to the Clinical Operations team's judgment. Dr. Tan asked whether the DoA should also cover procurement of laboratory supplies; Mr. Wong confirmed that this was already addressed in the Procurement Policy and would be cross-referenced.

Consensus: The Committee approved the revised DoA Policy, v2.0, subject to a final legal review. The policy will take effect on 1 April 2020. Mr. Wong will circulate the final version with the cross-reference to the Procurement Policy.

3. Update on Clinical Trial Site Qualification Criteria
   Dr. Chen provided an update on the site qualification criteria review. He noted that the current criteria (Policy CT-2018-009) did not explicitly address the use of electronic data capture (EDC) systems by sites. He proposed adding a requirement that sites must demonstrate proficiency in the EDC system used by the Consortium within 30 days of the site initiation visit.

Dr. Lim supported the proposal but suggested that the requirement be phased in to allow existing sites time to comply. Dr. Tan noted that the Consortium's own EDC system upgrade was scheduled for Q3 2020, and asked whether the new requirement should be aligned with that timeline. Dr. Chen agreed to revise the proposal accordingly and bring it back to the next meeting.

No formal vote was taken; the Committee agreed to defer the decision until the revised proposal is presented.

4. Any other business
   Dr. Tan reminded members that the annual staff performance review cycle would commence in May 2020. He asked each department head to submit their calibration schedules by 15 April 2020.

Meeting adjourned at 15:20.

Next meeting: 9 April 2020, 14:00, Meeting Room 4.

SUBJECT: Board of Directors Meeting Minutes — 22 April 2020

Date of meeting: 22 April 2020, 10:00–12:30
Venue: Boardroom, Level 3, MORC Headquarters (and via teleconference)
Chairperson: Prof. Alan Ng, Chairman of the Board
Attendees: Dr. S. Tan (Executive Director), Dr. M. Chen (Clinical Director), Dr. P. Lim (Head, Clinical Operations), Mr. K. Wong (Finance Director), Ms. R. Nair (HR Director), Prof. J. Lee (External Member), Dr. H. Yusof (External Member)
Secretariat: Ms. Grace Teo

1. Minutes of Previous Meeting
   The minutes of the meeting held on 20 January 2020 were confirmed as a true and accurate record.

2. Matters Arising
   Dr. Tan reported that the revised Delegation of Authority Policy v2.0 had been circulated to all committee members on 5 April 2020, following the legal review. The cross-reference to the Procurement Policy was included as agreed. The policy is now in effect.

3. Financial Report — Q1 2020
   Mr. Wong presented the unaudited financial results for the first quarter. Total revenue was within 2% of budget, with clinical trial-related income slightly ahead of forecast. Operating expenses were 4% below budget, largely due to reduced travel and meeting costs during the COVID-19 circuit breaker period. Mr. Wong noted that the impact of the pandemic on trial recruitment and monitoring activities remains uncertain, and he recommended that the Board approve a revised budget scenario for Q2–Q4.

Prof. Lee asked whether the Consortium had applied for any government support schemes, such as the Jobs Support Scheme. Mr. Wong confirmed that applications had been submitted and that the first tranche of support was received in March 2020.

Consensus: The Board approved the Q1 financial report and authorised Mr. Wong to develop a revised budget scenario for consideration at the next meeting.

4. COVID-19 Business Continuity Update
   Dr. Tan provided a verbal update on the Consortium's response to the pandemic. All non-essential on-site activities had been suspended since early April, and remote monitoring of trial sites had been implemented using existing EDC systems. The Clinical Operations team had developed a risk-based approach to determine which site visits could proceed, taking into account local government restrictions and patient safety.

Dr. Lim noted that some sites in Malaysia and Indonesia were experiencing delays in regulatory approvals for protocol amendments. The Board acknowledged these challenges and agreed that the Consortium should continue to engage with regulatory authorities to seek flexibility where possible.

5. Proposed Amendments to the Consortium Charter
   Prof. Ng raised the matter of the Charter's quorum requirements. The current Charter, adopted in 2018, requires a quorum of two-thirds of Board members for any meeting. Given the increasing use of teleconferencing and the possibility of extended travel restrictions, Prof. Ng proposed that the quorum requirement be amended to a simple majority, provided that at least one member is physically present at the Consortium's premises.

Dr. Yusof expressed concern that lowering the quorum could reduce the robustness of decision-making, particularly for matters requiring a two-thirds majority vote. Prof. Lee noted that the Charter already contains provisions for voting by electronic means and suggested that the proposed amendment be reviewed by the Governance Sub-Committee before a formal vote.

**MERIDIAN ONCOLOGY RESEARCH CONSORTIUM**
**CHARTER AND GOVERNANCE RECORDS**

**Addendum to Board Meeting Minutes – 14 May 2020 (continued)**

The Board noted the recommendation of the Governance Sub-Committee regarding the proposed amendment to Clause 9.2 (Quorum) of the Charter. The Sub-Committee met on 6 May 2020 and considered the proposal raised by Prof. Ng at the 16 April 2020 meeting. The Sub-Committee's report was circulated to all Board members on 8 May 2020.

The Sub-Committee recommended that the quorum requirement be revised from two-thirds of Board members to a simple majority, subject to the condition that at least one member is physically present at the Consortium's premises. This recommendation was reached by a majority of four to one, with Dr. Yusof dissenting. Dr. Yusof maintained his position that a lower quorum could weaken decision-making for matters requiring a two-thirds majority vote, such as amendments to the Charter itself or the removal of a Board member.

The Board discussed the report at length. Prof. Lee noted that the Charter's electronic voting provisions (Clause 9.4) had been used successfully for the first time during the 16 April 2020 meeting and that this experience supported the case for a lower quorum. Prof. Ng added that the ongoing COVID-19 situation made it impractical to convene two-thirds of members physically in the near term.

**Resolution 2020-07: The Board approved the amendment to Clause 9.2, effective 1 June 2020. The amended clause reads: "A quorum shall consist of a simple majority of Board members, provided that at least one member is physically present at the Consortium's premises or at a location designated by the Chair. Matters requiring a two-thirds majority vote under this Charter shall require the affirmative vote of two-thirds of all Board members, regardless of the number present."**

Dr. Yusof requested that his dissenting view be recorded in the minutes. The Chair confirmed that the dissent would be noted but that the resolution had passed by a vote of six to one.

---
